events.title: Python 3.0 released
events.summary: [Python] 3.0 shipped as an intentionally backward-incompatible cleanup of the language and standard library.
events.about: Same roles as [Python] 2 — scripting, web, data, [automation] — but with breaking fixes: proper [Unicode] strings, cleaner syntax (`print()` as function), and removed old APIs. Migration took years; today [Python] 3 is the only supported line for new work.

narrative.whyChosen: The [Python] 2→3 transition was one of the biggest ecosystem migrations in open-source history.
narrative.whyImportant: It fixed long-standing design warts (unicode strings, print as function, removed old APIs) at the cost of breakage.
narrative.problemSolved: [Python] 2 accumulated deprecated patterns that could not be fixed without breaking existing code.
